subject: Latency-first GPU strategy and capacity plan for Graybox Labs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Janet Lowe <janet@graybox.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Latency-first GPU strategy and capacity plan for Graybox Labs

Hi Janet,

Thanks again for the time today — good to align on the latency SLOs and expected QPS distribution. Per our conversation I pulled together a first-pass recommendation that prioritizes meeting your 200ms p95 tail for chat generation while keeping monthly committed spend under your stated target. High level summary below, full attachment is the PDF.

Key constraints you gave:
- Peak interactive QPS: 600 (US region), 30% of requests are long-context (>2k tokens)
- Average request size: 400 tokens in, ~120 tokens generated
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms; business-critical for search-chat features
- Budget: prefer a reserved capacity contract with predictable monthly commitment (flex to burst)

Initial recommendation (hybrid, latency-first):
1) Primary low-latency pool: H100 reserved cluster sized for 60% of peak QPS (360 QPS). Rationale: H100 gives the best sustained single-request latency for long-context, large models (up to 16k context with reasonable perf).
2) Secondary balanced pool: A100 reserved cluster sized for 30% (180 QPS) to handle steady mid-length requests and to absorb failover traffic. A100 is more cost-efficient per-token for many of your medium-length generation patterns.
3) Burst/concurrency pool: L4 on demand (burstable) configured for embedding and short-chat bursts (~60 QPS nominal). L4s are cost-effective for high-concurrency, short prompt workloads and for batched embedding jobs.

Operational notes:
- KV/prefix caching on H100 for long conversations will save ~25% of compute and improve p95.
- Route long-context requests preferentially to H100; fallback policy to A100 after 300ms, then to L4 for best-effort short responses.
- Reserve commit: recommended initial committed capacity = 6 H100 cards (DGX-style allocation equivalent), 8 A100 cards, with an L4 auto-burst pool.

I've attached a short worksheet (CSV) you can drop your real traffic into — will update numbers after you send the anonymized sample we requested. Next steps: if this aligns, I can loop in our finance lead and send a pilot PO for 30 days of guaranteed capacity + credits to validate perf.

Attachment: latency-first-hybrid-plan-v1.pdf (2 pages)

Cheers,
Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Janet Lowe <janet@graybox.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Graybox Labs Procurement <procurement@graybox.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency-first GPU strategy and capacity plan for Graybox Labs

Rafael — thanks for the quick turnaround. This looks promising. A couple of clarifications before we run the CSV through our ops team:

1) On the H100 sizing: are those 6 cards assuming model quantization (8-bit) or FP16 runtimes? We use an internal LLM (fine-tuned LlamaX) that has a memory footprint closer to uncompressed FP16.
2) For A100 vs H100 fallbacks: what is your expected p95 delta (ms) for 4k-context requests between H100 and A100? Our internal acceptance test will include 4k and 8k contexts.
3) Procurement asks if you can do a 30-day pilot with a cap on overage; we need predictable spend for this quarter.

I'll attach a redacted sample of our traffic tonight. Procurement: please confirm..

—Janet
VP Product, Graybox Labs

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Latency-first GPU strategy and capacity plan for Graybox Labs

Team — forwarding Graybox questions. Short tech checklist and numbers we should validate before committing numbers to the customer:

- Memory assumptions: their fine-tuned LlamaX suggests FP16 model ~80GB VRAM requirement at 8k context. If so, H100 80GB card (H100 80GB SXM) is required for no-split inference. If they are using model sharding + kv offload, we can support on A100 but expect a ~25-40% latency penalty at p95.
- Quantization: if they can take 8-bit quantization (Q4_K_M or 4-bit dynamic <depending on accuracy tests), effective memory drops and A100 fitment improves. Ask for a holdout eval set to test quantized model accuracy.
- Latency expectations: rough internal benchmarks say for 4k contexts: H100 p95 ~180ms; A100 p95 ~260-320ms (depends on batching, KV cache hit rate). 8k contexts: H100 p95 ~300-350ms; A100 p95 ~450-600ms. These are ballpark — need their exact model to run a 2-hour perf run.
- Routing plan: primary->H100, failover->A100 (no model fallback unless we've validated quantized variant), short requests->L4 with batching logic and prefix caching disabled for embeddings.

Can one of you run a quick simulation using the sample CSV when Janet sends it? I want a tight one-page note for procurement that describes a pilot: 30 days, 50% committed discount, 30% credit on overage for the pilot period, and a bump option to a 3-month committed contract.

Rafael

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency-first GPU strategy and capacity plan for Graybox Labs

Quick simulation notes after a pass through the redacted CSV Janet uploaded this morning (attached):

- Observed peak concurrent long-context sessions: ~210 (not 1800) — their earlier top-line estimate looked conservative; this reduces H100 capacity needs materially.
- Revised sizing (to hit p95 <= 200ms assuming our caching):
  * H100 reserved: equivalent of 4 H100 80GB GPUs (handles ~360k tokens/minute with cache hit 30%)
  * A100 reserved: equivalent of 6 A100 80GB GPUs (steady background traffic and failover)
  * L4 burst: autoscale group with 12 L4 instances for short-chat and embedding spikes
- Cost delta: rough committed-monthly estimate (net of pilot discounts): H100 cluster ~$85k/month; A100 cluster ~$45k/month; L4 burst nominal $6k/month (autoscale).
- Risk: if they cannot accept 8-bit quantization and insist on FP16 for 8k-context models, we must provision more H100 headroom (plus network bandwidth for sharded models). Recommend a two-week bench test to lock model footprint.

I'll prepare a one-page deck and a short pricing note for Rafael/Marissa to share with procurement.

- Dev

Attachment: graybox_analysis_run1.csv (sample-derived), note: internal numbers are estimate-only

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Latency-first GPU strategy and capacity plan for Graybox Labs

Janet — thanks for the sample and the quick follow-up. Based on Dev's simulation and our internal perf priors, here's a compact pilot proposal you can take to procurement: 

Pilot summary (30 days)
- Reserved: 4x H100 (80GB) + 6x A100 (80GB) dedicated to Graybox in US-east region.
- Burst: L4 autoscale for short-chat and embed spikes, capped at 12 instances during pilot.
- Pricing: 50% committed discount on listed capacity for the 30-day pilot; 30% overage credit on any usage beyond the cap (credit applied to the following invoice). Estimated net pilot cost: $70k (approx).
- Acceptance tests: we will run a two-day perf window with your holdout set (4k and 8k contexts) during week 2. Passing criteria: p95 <= 200ms for 80% of sampled requests; no more than 5% request failures under load.
- Data/security: private VPC connectivity, audit logs enabled for pilot; we will restrict model artifacts to your tenant and will not use them for model training.

Next steps if this is acceptable:
1) Procurement confirms PO cap and signs pilot addendum (DocuSign link in HubSpot).
2) We provision pilot capacity within 3 business days and run a smoke perf test.
3) Two-week validation window; we iterate routing thresholds and quantization flags with Dev.

If procurement wants adjusted spend caps or a shorter pilot window, we can flex — Marissa/Finance can weigh in on exact credit terms.

Looking forward — let me know and I'll push a draft pilot SOW and send the DocuSign.

Best,
Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
